questions.answer: No. Solo you take all 4 cards of your hand, then keep only those you want, paying the keep cost (1 insight tier 1, 2 tier 2, then 5 credits per missing insight) for each kept; discard the rest.

Yes. The token was not spent on the factory, and one hardening token on a hex with both your facility and your node can save either, once; you may keep it for the second. Threat destruction goes through the protection order, so you can spend it then (if the factory was destroyed, the token is assumed still on the hex).
questions.where: 13 protection order and the paragraph after it
questions.unsure: Whether a hardening token placed 'on a station or factory' leaves with that facility when the troop destroys it; the book says the token is 'on the hex' but never says it survives.

questions.answer: No. A troop landing does nothing to ambassadors until it marches; in the march, its step on that hex removes one ambassador (players choose whose).

7 / 3 = 2 each, remainder 1. The remainder goes to the lowest-numbered station that isn't the adversary's (and isn't firewalled). So the adversary's station gets 2, the lower-numbered of the other two gets 3, the other gets 2. Any landing on a hex with players' ambassadors cancels one for one.
Onto the project costing 4 (the cheapest by printed cost, however full), even though the 6-cost project is one short.
2 drones: 1 on each of the two bases of its own country, if those bases have room (max 2 a base; a full base takes none). Each ambassador on the factory would stop one.
Yes. An open-land target is an open hex with no base, station, factory or land corruption, 'a node on it or not'.
questions.unsure: Which corrupt number applies (2 for a node hex 'whatever else is there', or 3 for open land), and whether reaching 2 only loses the node (marker) or corrupts the land (token).

questions.answer: Stops adversary troops moving onto, landing on (they stay in supply) or striking a hex with the Protector's node; marching troops path around it. Does not stop corruption, war (drones), threats, agents, or production: an adversary factory on that hex still makes its troop there, which then marches off.
questions.unsure: How 'strike a hex' applies to a target facility next to (not on) the Protector's node.

questions.answer: It is the Militarist adversary board's rule (step 6 of the adversary's turn), answering the Protector's Wall. In each country where the Protector has a node, Muster 1 on that country's lowest-numbered adversary or neutral factory, never a player's and never a city; with no such factory, none lands. If the Protector's node is on that factory's hex, it stays in the supply. Level 2+ adds 1 troop.
questions.where: 6 Militarist rules and step 6; 5 Wall; 21 Muster

questions.answer: 3 adversary troops in each country (2 + 1 level surcharge), landing one at a time on the lowest-numbered factory (any owner), else the lowest-numbered city, else none. A Wall-blocked or prohibited landing stays in the supply and does not move on.
questions.unsure: Whether all three stack on the same factory; the text implies yes.

questions.answer: No. Every contact is one for one: an agent landing or moving onto ambassadors removes one with itself, and an ambassador arriving on agents removes one with itself. Claim/Liberate on a site with agents is paid from your supply for that reason. (A Convert card resolves leftovers the same way.)
questions.where: 8 Ambassadors meet agents; 8 Claim and Liberate; 16 Convert

questions.answer: Shelter lasts action phase to cleanup only, so not the adversary's turn; it covers only one country; it stops only destruction of nodes/facilities through the protection order, so cubes still change hands (a site still corrupts), ambassadors are still removed, and a node you give up to pay something is still lost.

gaps: Hardening token vs its facility: Harden puts it 'on a station or factory', 13 calls it 'on the hex'; never says whether it survives the facility's destruction (the G3-2 case).
Open land with a node under Corrupt open land: which corrupt number (2 or 3) and which result (land corruption token, or only node loss and a marker).
Corrupted city factory growth when no free zone has an agent on or next to it: 'if it can' with no fallback.
Wall 'strike a hex': unclear for a facility next to, not on, the Protector's node, and for another player's facility on that hex.
Compute goes to the cheapest project by printed cost however full: counterintuitive and has no example; a reader will expect it to finish the nearly full project.
Level table compute income 4 to 22 between levels 1 and 2 with no explanation; reads as a typo.
overall: The book is clear and well ordered for a hobby gamer: the round table, the near/nearest split, the protection order and the worked examples answered almost every question I put to it. The weak spots are edge cases where two rules meet on one hex (a node on open land under Corrupt, a hardening token outliving its facility, Wall against adjacent strikes) and a few counterintuitive rules (compute to the cheapest project) stated without examples. Density, not missing rules, is the main cost: several key exceptions live in parentheticals that need a second read.
